facts.title: Breton Won Over
facts.text: In 1944, André Breton discovered Arshile Gorky's paintings and hailed him as a true Surrealist.
facts.spoken: In 1944 in New York, André Breton hailed him as a true Surrealist.

facts.title: Khorkom
facts.text: Born Vosdanik Manoug Adoian in the Ottoman Empire, the future painter grew up on the shores of Lake Van.
facts.spoken: Born near Lake Van, his name was then Vosdanik Manoug Adoian.

facts.text: Forced to flee in 1915, he saw his mother die of starvation in Yerevan during the winter of 1918–1919.
facts.spoken: After fleeing in 1915, he lost his mother to starvation in Yerevan.

facts.text: Arriving in the United States at the age of sixteen in 1920, he adopted the name Arshile Gorky in New York.
facts.spoken: Arriving in 1920 at the age of sixteen, he took the name Arshile Gorky.

facts.title: The Artist and His Mother
facts.text: He worked patiently on this double portrait inspired by a childhood photograph taken in Van.
facts.spoken: He painted this portrait inspired by a childhood photo.

facts.title: An Innovative Style
facts.text: A friend of Willem de Kooning, he invented biomorphic forms that paved the way for Abstract Expressionism.
facts.spoken: With Willem de Kooning, he paved the way for Abstract Expressionism.

facts.title: Forty-four years
facts.text: Passing away at forty-four, his work is now exhibited at the Centre Pompidou and Tate.
facts.spoken: Passing away at forty-four, his paintings are admired worldwide.

ytTitle: Arshile Gorky: From the Armenian Genocide to the Heights of Modern Art
ytLead: Refugee in the United States after the 1915 genocide, Vosdanik Adoian became the celebrated painter Arshile Gorky. He established himself as one of the founding fathers of Abstract Expressionism.
